review.title: A Lead Given Away, Then a Gift Handed Back
review.summary: Black, the 20k, won by resignation after GPT-6.1 Sol had been ahead early on. White's best stretch came after turn 7, when the lead stood at -4.4. From turn 10 on, its moves gave points away, and the 19.2-point loss on turn 16 and the 37.9-point loss on turn 26 left it far behind. The 20k blundered too, but never enough to give the lead back, and White resigned after turn 33.

moments.text: C4 reaches the same line as C3 and C5 on the left, but it lost 4.9 points and flipped the lead from -1.8 to +3.1 for Black. The engine preferred D4. White had been ahead, and this was the first move after which it was not.
H7 pushed against Black's G8 and H8 stones. It lost 19.2 points and took the lead from +5.6 to +24.8. The engine's choice was H8, the point Black played next. A close game became a lopsided one here.

J3 is White's worst move of the game, losing 37.9 points and sending the lead from +35.2 to +73.1. The engine wanted D7, in the middle of the board. Instead the move added a stone to the group on the right edge, which was already tied up with H3, H4 and H5.

The 20k answered with F4, which lost 38.7 points, the worst move on either side. It cut the lead from +73.1 to +34.4, almost exactly undoing J3. Black was still comfortably ahead, and the engine's choice here was B2.

E6 lost 34.1 points and the lead went from +37.9 to +72.0. It extended the stones at D5 and D6 while Black's F4, F5 and E4 held the centre. The engine's choice was B2. Black's next move, F5, lost 36.9 points but left the lead at +35.2, and White resigned after that.

audit.reason: All the code (command 33's board parser, group/liberty/region inspector and replay of actual moves, plus the apply_patch log/SGF/memory writes and file reads) only inspected the current or recorded positions and kept records. Nothing looped over candidate moves, played out continuations or ranked moves; every play() call carried a manually chosen move.
